{{widget}}
The '''Color Curve''' object type allows various addon functionality with [[Secret Values|secrets]], that would otherwise not be possible, for example coloring the health bar based on the remaining health of the unit. The generic {{apitype|CurveObject}} handles other cases. Create one using {{api|C_CurveUtil.CreateColorCurve()}}.

==Example==
The reference example.
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua" line=1>
-- The following example creates a color curve that when evaluated will
-- produce a red color between [0 and 30%) health, yellow between [30 and 70%)
-- health, and green above that.
--
-- We use a "Step" curve type here to disable interpolation between colors
-- based on the percentage. If no type is explicitly configured, the default
-- is to perform Linear interpolation (which is applied individually per color
-- channel).
--
-- AddPoint takes an 'x' and 'y' value; the 'x' should be a percentage scaled
-- between [0-1] and the 'y' should be a ColorMixin structure. Curves support
-- a maximum of 256 points.

local curve = C_CurveUtil.CreateColorCurve();
curve:SetType(Enum.LuaCurveType.Step);
curve:AddPoint(0.0, CreateColor(1, 0, 0, 1));
curve:AddPoint(0.3, CreateColor(1, 1, 0, 1));
curve:AddPoint(0.7, CreateColor(0, 1, 0, 1));

-- Alternatively, there's a SetPoints API which takes a vector of point
-- structures:

-- curve:SetPoints({ { x = 0, y = CreateColor(...) }, ... });

-- To evaluate the curve and get a unit health color out of it, use the new
-- UnitHealthPercent API:

local usePredicted = true;
local color = UnitHealthPercent("target", usePredicted, curve);
statusBar:GetStatusBarTexture():SetVertexColor(color:GetRGB());
</syntaxhighlight>

Full example with an updating statusbar for yourself; uses linear interpolation.
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua" line=1>
local curve = C_CurveUtil.CreateColorCurve()
curve:SetType(Enum.LuaCurveType.Linear)
curve:AddPoint(0.0, CreateColor(1, 0, 0))
curve:AddPoint(0.3, CreateColor(1, 1, 0))
curve:AddPoint(0.7, CreateColor(0, 1, 0))

local statusBar = CreateFrame("StatusBar", nil, UIParent)
statusBar:SetPoint("CENTER", -150, -50)
statusBar:SetSize(144, 17)
statusBar:SetStatusBarTexture("Interface/TargetingFrame/UI-StatusBar")
statusBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, 1)

local function OnEvent(self, event, unit)
	local usePredicted = true
	local color = UnitHealthPercent(unit, usePredicted, curve)
	local value = UnitHealthPercent(unit, usePredicted, CurveConstants.ZeroToOne)
	statusBar:GetStatusBarTexture():SetVertexColor(color:GetRGB())
	statusBar:SetValue(value)
	print(format("%s, health=%.2f, r=%.2f, g=%.2f, b=%.2f", unit, value, color:GetRGB()))
end

local f = CreateFrame("Frame")
f:RegisterUnitEvent("UNIT_HEALTH", "player")
f:SetScript("OnEvent", OnEvent)
</syntaxhighlight>
